summary.text: Ruben Cruz II is a small-business owner and community advocate who describes himself as the founding director of a health, wellness and arts programming firm. He is the Republican and Queens United Party candidate for Assembly District 38 and previously ran unsuccessfully for Assembly District 24 (2024) and State Senate District 16 (2022). According to his campaign website, he is running on protecting homeowners and seniors, rebuilding the local economy and cutting hidden fees.

paragraphs.text: Cruz graduated from Richmond Hill High School and holds a bachelor's degree in Theatre and Dance from CUNY Queens College (1999).
He says he is the founding director of a firm that has provided health, wellness, and arts and culture programming in New York City since 2006, and describes himself as a "Community Architect."

During the COVID-19 pandemic he founded the Queens Pet Pantry, a pet-supply distribution project; he says it was created in collaboration with city agencies and animal-welfare groups and that its data-management system was later adopted by the ASPCA. His campaign website says his team managed the Queens Pet Pantry and community-center relocations.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he described working with the Community Agency for Senior Citizens on elder abuse and elder justice with the State Office of Victim Services.

He lives in Richmond Hill, Queens, and serves on Queens Community Board 9. Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the Latin American Intercultural Alliance, the Central Queens Republican Club and Queens Libertarians.
Cruz ran as the Republican, Conservative and Independence Party candidate for State Senate District 16 in 2022, losing to incumbent John Liu 57.7% to 42.2%.
In 2024 he ran as the Republican, Conservative and Common Sense Party candidate for Assembly District 24, losing to incumbent David Weprin 61.1% to 35.1%.
The 2026 Republican primary for Assembly District 38 was canceled and Cruz advanced to the general election on the Republican and Queens United Party lines.
